project.objective: Who were the children of Lewis Washington Ogletree, born 1882 in Georgia, who married Mattie Pearcy in 1905 in Spalding County, Georgia and later moved to Chicago, Illinois?

questions.question: Who were all the children born to Lewis Washington Ogletree (b. 1882, Georgia) and his wife Mattie Pearcy (m. 1905, Spalding County, Georgia)?
questions.rationale: This is the primary objective: identifying the complete set of children of Lewis Washington Ogletree and Mattie Pearcy. Key record types include U.S. census schedules (1910–1940) showing household composition in Georgia and later Chicago, Illinois; Georgia birth records; Illinois birth records; Cook County vital records; and obituaries/death certificates that may name children as survivors. The couple's documented move to Chicago opens access to Illinois records alongside Georgia sources.

items.rationale: Lewis and Mattie married in Spalding County in 1905. The 1910 US census is the first census after their marriage and will enumerate Lewis, Mattie, and any children born through April 1910 — up to 4-5 years of children. This is the highest-probability single source for an early list of children. The 1910 Georgia census is well-indexed on FamilySearch. Per loc_001, the family is African American; the enumerator's race column will help confirm the correct household. Three persons already in the tree (Nellie Mae Ogletree, Lewis Ogletree, Harriett Haygood) may appear as children here.

items.jurisdiction: Spalding County, Georgia; Cook County, Illinois
items.rationale: The 1920 census will show children still in the household 10-15 years into the marriage. The family may still be in Spalding County or may have already migrated to Chicago. Per loc_001, the 1920 Spalding County census volume (imageGroup 004300135) is 0% indexed on FamilySearch — browse-only; Ancestry has it indexed. Search Ancestry for Lewis Ogletree in both Georgia and Illinois to locate the household wherever the family resided in January 1920.

By 1930 the family is expected to be in Chicago. The 1930 census will list all children still in the household, with ages that help calculate birth years. Per loc_001, the Spalding County 1930 census is also 0% indexed on FamilySearch; search both Spalding County, GA (if migration was later than expected) and Cook County, IL on FamilySearch or Ancestry. The 1930 census is indexed on FamilySearch for Illinois.

The 1940 US census is free and fully indexed on FamilySearch. By 1940 most children would be teenagers or adults; older children may have their own households nearby. Searching for the Lewis Ogletree household AND each known child's household in Cook County in 1940 will capture children who had moved out but remained in Chicago. Children still at home will be listed with the parents.

The Social Security NUMIDENT (United States, Social Security Numerical Identification Files, 1936-2007; FS collection 5000016) lists every person who applied for a Social Security number. Children of Lewis and Mattie born roughly 1906-1930 would have applied for SS in their 20s-30s (1940s-1960s). The NUMIDENT entry gives: birth date, birth place, parents' names (on the SS-5 application), and often death date. This is the single most powerful national cross-check for identifying and confirming children. Also search the Social Security Death Index (FS collection 1202535) for death dates of known children.

World War II draft registration cards (FamilySearch collection 1880573, Georgia; national via Ancestry) cover men born between 1877 and 1897 (1st registration) and 1886-1897 and 1897-1927 (later registrations), capturing virtually all adult men in 1940. Sons of Lewis and Mattie born c.1906-1927 would appear. Each card lists: full name, birth date and place, employer, and next of kin — often the father or mother, confirming the Lewis Ogletree parentage link. Lewis Ogletree (L5D9-KXT already in tree) is a candidate son; his draft card, if found, will name his birth date and parents.

Children who died in Georgia before or shortly after migration will appear in Georgia death certificates. Search: (a) Georgia Deaths 1914-1927 (FS collection 1320969, indexed & images) and (b) Georgia Deaths 1928-1943 (FS collection 1385727, indexed & images). Per loc_001, death records for African Americans were often filed in separate indexes — search both the main index and any 'colored' sub-series. A Georgia death certificate gives: name, age/birth date, parents' names, cause of death, and place of burial — all useful for confirming parentage and birth year.

Georgia County Delayed Birth Records 1870-1960 (FS collection 3438747, index & images) capture affidavits filed by Georgians who needed a birth certificate but lacked one — common for African Americans born before statewide registration (1919). Each affidavit names the applicant's birth date and place, parents' names, and witnesses. Children of Lewis and Mattie born 1906-1919 are likely candidates for delayed birth filings. Also check Georgia Births and Christenings 1754-1960 (FS collection 1674802, index only) for any christening records. Per loc_001, no statewide birth registration existed before 1919 in Georgia.

Children who married in Spalding County before the family migrated to Chicago will appear in county marriage records. Per loc_001, African American marriage records in Spalding County were kept in separate 'colored' volumes: vol. F (1903-1910, imageGroup 007718973, 100% indexed), vol. G (1910-1917, imageGroup 007718974, 100% indexed), vol. H (1917-1923, imageGroup 007718975, 100% indexed), and vol. I (1923-1933, imageGroup 007718976, 100% indexed). Search for the surname Ogletree in all four volumes. Harriett Haygood (K45Y-CC5, already in tree) may have married a Haygood in this county — her marriage record would confirm parentage. Also search the statewide Georgia County Marriages 1785-1950 (FS collection 1927197).

Obituaries for Lewis Washington Ogletree and Mattie Pearcy Ogletree in Chicago newspapers are among the highest-value sources for this question: they characteristically name ALL surviving children with their cities of residence, and sometimes deceased children as well. Search Chicago Defender (the primary African American newspaper in Chicago, 1905-present) and Chicago Tribune via Newspapers.com / GenealogyBank / ProQuest on Ancestry and other platforms. A Cook County locality guide (not yet created) will identify the full suite of Illinois vital record collections; for now, this item targets newspaper obituaries and death notices as the most actionable external source. Note: Lewis and Mattie's Cook County death certificates (when found) will also name an informant — usually a child — and may list survivors.

Primary pli_001 search: 1910 US Census, Spalding County GA, surname Ogletree + Lewis. Top hit: L W Ogletree, District 1065, matchScore 0.767, already attachedToSubject. Record ARK: ark:/61903/1:1:MLLW-J7F. Household batchNumber N03341-2 noted for enumeration.

Batch enumeration page 1 (offset 0): batchNumber N03341-2, surname Ogletree. L W Ogletree household contains: Lewis (head, b.1882 GA), Mattie (wife, b.1886 TN), Annie (daughter, b.1908 GA), Guyson (son, b.1909 GA). Two children identified.
Batch enumeration page 2 (offset 20): batchNumber N03341-2, surname Ogletree. No additional children of Lewis and Mattie identified in this page.
pli_002 search 1: surname Ogletree, givenName L W, 1920 census, Cook County IL. Zero results. Family may not yet have migrated to Chicago by 1920, or may be indexed under full name.

pli_002 search 2: surname Ogletree, givenName Lewis, birthYear 1879-1885, birthPlace Georgia, census, United States. 37 results across all census years but NO confident 1920 census match. Top ranked match was 1950 census (Lewis W Ogletree, Chicago, matchScore 0.896, already attached) and 1930 census (Louis Ogletree, Chicago, matchScore 0.528, already attached). Spalding County 1920 census is browse-only on FamilySearch (0% indexed per loc_001); Ancestry search still needed.

1930 US Census, Cook County IL search for Lewis Ogletree. Key finds: (1) 'Louis Ogletree' (b.1885 GA, Negro, married, matchScore 0.528, already attached to subject) in Howard D Chapman household — likely Lewis Washington Ogletree, name transcribed as 'Louis'. (2) Hattie L Ogletree household (ark 1YZP-QKB) contains Lewis W Ogletree (b.1916 GA) and Louise Ogletree (b.1910 GA) — two previously unidentified potential children of Lewis and Mattie. Hattie L Ogletree (head, b.1900 GA) may be a daughter or sibling of Lewis; relationship to subject requires person-evidence evaluation.

pli_004 search 1: Lewis Ogletree, 1940 census, Cook County IL. No confident match for the father (b.1882 GA). Key find: 'Lewis Ogeltree' (b.1917 GA, Negro, Single) in 'Household of Hattie Ogeltreel' — the son Lewis Jr. seen in 1930 Hattie household, still living with Hattie in 1940. Father not located in this search.
pli_004 search 2: 'Louis' variant (from 1930 transcription), 1940 census, Cook County IL, birth year 1879-1886. Zero results.

pli_004 search 3: L W Ogletree, b.1879-1886, Georgia, 1940 US census. Three results, none matching the subject. Father not located in 1940 census via FamilySearch; may be indexed under a different name form or living outside Cook County. Note: 1950 census confirms he was alive in Chicago by 1950.

pli_005 NUMIDENT search 1: Ogletree, born 1905-1925, Georgia. 1878 total matches — too diffuse for the subject matcher (scores all below 0.01). Notable: James Ogletree (b.10 Mar 1922, Griffin/Spalding, GA, Black, d.1999) born in Spalding County; Irene Ogletre Ogletree (b.26 Oct 1910, GA, Black, Lansing Cook IL). No confident match for any known child.
pli_005 NUMIDENT search 2: Ogletree, givenName Guyson (the son's rare name). Returns middle-initial G records only; 'Guyson' not indexed in this form in the NUMIDENT.

pli_005 NUMIDENT search 3: Annie Ogletree, b.1906-1912. 100 results; most entries lack birth place. Top hit Annie B Ogletree (b.5 Jul 1908, Florida) not born in Georgia. Cannot confirm any as Lewis and Mattie's daughter Annie without additional corroborating facts.

pli_006 search 1: Guyson Ogletree, Georgia WWII draft (collection 1880573). Only result is Luther G Ogletree (b.1926, Fayette GA) — not our Guyson. Name may not be indexed, or Guyson may have moved before draft age.

pli_006 search 2: Lewis Ogletree, military, born 1910-1920, Georgia. Key finds: (1) 'Lewis Washington Ogletree' (b.16 Apr 1914, Griffin/Spalding GA, Negro, residence Chicago) IL WWII draft — a son named after his father, born Spalding County, living in Chicago (ark QPZW-ZVNT). (2) 'Lewis Ogletree' (b.19 Nov 1912, Spalding GA, Griffin residence) GA WWII draft (ark Q2Q8-MJV9). (3) 'Lewis Davis Ogletree' (b.21 Feb 1919, Griffin/Spalding GA) GA WWII draft + discharge (ark Q2Q8-MJ2S). Multiple Lewis Ogletrees from Spalding County warrant further investigation.

Georgia Deaths 1914-1927 (collection 1320969). 20 Ogletree death records returned, mostly older or White Ogletrees unrelated to Lewis and Mattie. One notable: 'Marry Ogletree' (b.1907, Black, d.10 Oct 1924, LaGrange, Troup GA) — born 1907 in Georgia, race Black; conceivably a child of Lewis and Mattie but birthplace is Troup County not Spalding. No confirmed children of Lewis and Mattie Ogletree found in this collection. Logging pli_007 part 1; part 2 (collection 1385727, 1928-1943) follows.

Georgia Deaths 1928-1943 (collection 1385727). 185 total matches, 20 examined. Notable: 'Louise Ogletree' (b.1908, Race:Colored, d.22 May 1940, Thomaston, Upson GA) — b.1908 Black female, born year consistent with a child of Lewis and Mattie (married 1905); 'Jim Henry Ogletree' (b.1906, Black, d.29 Oct 1928, Spalding GA) — b.1906 in Spalding area, died in Spalding County, Black male — strong candidate as a child of Lewis and Mattie. Most other results are from Troup, Meriwether, Heard counties unrelated to the Spalding family. Both Louise and Jim Henry warrant record reads.

Georgia County Delayed Birth Records 1870-1960 (collection 3438747). 41 total matches searching Ogletree surname with father surname Ogletree, birth years 1905-1930. All top results show relativeTerms.father.status: unknown (index silent about father) or absent (different father named). Results from Murray, Gwinnett, Heard counties — none from Spalding County visible. Lower-score results are persons named Ogletree who appear as relatives on other persons' records. No confirmed children of Lewis and Mattie Ogletree found in this collection.

Georgia County Marriages 1785-1950, statewide (collection 1927197), 1920-1940. 188 matches, 20 examined. No marriage dates or county visible in index stubs. Need to search the specific Spalding County colored volumes (imageGroups 007718973-007718976) to identify children of Lewis and Mattie who married in Spalding County. Notable: 'Tillman Ogletree and Louise Phillip'; 'Synn Ogletree and Lena Williams' — require record reads to determine county and parentage. Searching Spalding-specific colored volumes as next step.

Spalding County colored marriage vol. F (imageGroup 007718973), 1903-1910. 13 results, all examined. Key find: 'L W Ogletree and Mattie Pearcy' (MarriageLicense 1 Nov 1905, Spalding GA) — Lewis Sr. and Mattie's own marriage record, corroborates the 1905 marriage date and place. Other Ogletrees appear to be collateral relatives (Will, George, Wiley, Otis, Nannie, Jessie, Hattie McKibbin Ogletree). No confirmed children of Lewis and Mattie found in this volume.

Spalding County colored marriage vol. G (imageGroup 007718974), 1910-1917. 19 results, all examined. No index dates visible. Names include Nudie Gay Ogletree, Preston R, Lucille, Willie (marrying Mattie Darden), Earl, Bertha May, T B Ogletree — none match known children of Lewis and Mattie born 1906-1917. Children of Lewis and Mattie would be at most 11 years old by 1917 and unlikely to appear in this volume.

Spalding County colored marriage vol. H (imageGroup 007718975), 1917-1923. 13 results, all examined. Key find: 'Annie L Ogletree marrying Willie C Berry' — Annie Ogletree born ~1908 would be 9-15 years old in 1917-1923; this may be a daughter of Lewis and Mattie (I2 in tree). Other names: Martin Ogletree and Annie White, Fred Ogletree and Laura Butler, Easter Ogletree, Edward James Ogletree and Annie Lee Owens, Willie Lee Ogletree. Record read needed for Annie L Ogletree to confirm parentage.

Spalding County colored marriage vol. I (imageGroup 007718976), 1923-1933. 19 results, all examined. Key find: 'L W Ogletree and Ada Morris' — an L W Ogletree married Ada Morris in this volume (1923-1933). If this is Lewis Sr. (b.1882), he would be ~41-51 years old, suggesting Mattie may have died or they separated before this marriage. This could explain household arrangements seen in 1930 census. Record read needed to confirm identity. Also: Julia Ogletree (marrying Boissie Lewis), Gertrude Ogletree (marrying Wm Brooks), Daisy Ogletree, Hazel Ogletree, Clyde Ogletree (female, marrying Robert Head). None confirmed as children of Lewis and Mattie without further investigation.

Annie L Ogletree married Willie C Berry, 17 Feb 1920, Spalding, Georgia. No parent names on the marriage record. Annie born ~1908 per 1910 census — she would be ~12 years old at this marriage (historically possible). This may confirm the Annie Ogletree (I2) identified in the 1910 census. Delegate to extraction.

L W Ogletree married Ada Morris, 6 Jan 1930, Spalding, Georgia. No parent names or ages on the marriage record. L W Ogletree in the Spalding County colored volume — likely Lewis Washington Ogletree Sr. (b.1882). Marriage date of Jan 1930 predates the April 1930 census where 'Louis Ogletree' appeared as boarder in Chicago. Suggests Lewis Sr. may have married again in January 1930 before moving to Chicago, OR this is Lewis Jr. (b.1914) who would be 15-16 years old — possible but young. Delegate to extraction.

Jim Henry Ogletree (b.1906, d.29 Oct 1928, Spalding GA, Black, Single). ELIMINATES as child of Lewis and Mattie: death certificate names father as John Ogletree and mother as Lizzie Bussey — not Lewis Washington Ogletree and Mattie Pearcy. Jim Henry belongs to a different Ogletree family in Spalding County.

Louise Ogletree (b.1908 GA, d.22 May 1940, Thomaston, Upson GA, Colored). ELIMINATES as child of Lewis and Mattie: death certificate names father as Sun Smoot and mother as Julia Oglebut (likely transcription of Ogletree). This Louise is a child of an Ogletree woman named Julia who married a Smoot — not a daughter of Lewis and Mattie. The Louise found in the 1930 Chicago census (in Hattie's household) is a different person and remains under investigation.

L W Ogletree and Mattie Pearcy marriage record, 1 Nov 1905, Spalding, Georgia (Spalding County colored marriage vol. F). Confirms the marriage date and Spalding County location. L W Ogletree = Lewis Washington Ogletree Sr. (b.1882, GW4W-DTG). Delegate to extraction to corroborate marriage date/place already in tree.

Original WWII draft registration card image for Lewis Washington Ogletree, 16 Oct 1940. CRITICAL FINDING: Field 8 (Relationship) reads 'AUNT' for Hattie Ogletree — the FamilySearch index generalized this as 'Relative'. This confirms: (1) Lewis Washington Ogletree Jr. (b.16 Apr 1914, Griffin GA) is a nephew of Hattie Ogletree, meaning Hattie is a sibling of either Lewis Sr. or Mattie Pearcy; (2) Given Hattie's b.~1900 GA and the Ogletree surname, she is almost certainly a sibling of Lewis Sr. (b.1882 GA); (3) This eliminates Hattie L Ogletree as a child of Lewis and Mattie. Both Lewis Jr. and Hattie shared the same address (4815 Vincennes Ave., Chicago) at time of registration. Registrant's full name on card: LEWIS WASHINGTON OGLETREE. Height 6-1, Weight 147, Race: Negro, Complexion: Dark brown. Image saved as images/ark_61903_3_1_3Q9M-CSTM-R9C6-2.jpg."

Search for Mattie Ogletree death records, United States, birth 1880-1895. 420 total matches, 50 examined. Ranked matches against GW4W-DTG scored very low (max 0.0012 — all effectively zero). No death record found for Mattie Pearcy Ogletree. Several co-occurrence hits where 'Mattie Ogletree' appears as informant/relative on Georgia death records (1914-1927, 1928-1943) — these are informant appearances, not her own death record. Mattie's death, if any, may have occurred in Illinois (not yet searched) or her death is not indexed. This negative result does not establish she was alive in 1930 but means no FamilySearch evidence of her death was found.

Search for Lewis Ogletree in 1900 census, Georgia, birth 1878-1886. 5 results, all examined. Top match (matchScore 0.433, already attached to GW4W-DTG): 'Lewis Ogletree' (b. August 1885, Black, Single, District 1065, Spalding County GA) in 'Household of L W Ogletree' (ark:/61903/1:1:M3V7-51R). This is Lewis Sr. in his father's household in Spalding County. Record already attached to GW4W-DTG but not yet extracted into research.json. Reading household to identify siblings including possible Hattie.

Search for Hattie Ogletree in 1900 census, GA, birth 1896-1904. Only 1 result returned: 'Bob H Ogletree' (b. Feb 1899, Male, Black, Troup County GA) — not Hattie. Hattie Ogletree (b.~1900) may not have been born yet at the June 1900 census date or is indexed under a different name. Negative result does not disprove existence.

1900 US Census, Militia District 1065, Spalding County GA. Household of L W Ogletree (b. Aug 1856, Black, married). Lewis Sr. (GW4W-DTG) appears as 'Lucas/Lewis Ogletree' (b. August 1885, single, Black). Household members (all Black, Spalding County GA): (1) L W Ogletree [head, b.1856, father of Lewis Sr.]; (2) Mattie Ogletree [wife, b.1856, mother of Lewis Sr. -- same given name as Lewis Sr.'s wife Mattie Pearcy, which explains name confusion in research]; (3) Lewis/Lucas Ogletree [b.Aug 1885]; (4) Samuel Ogletree [b.Jun 1886]; (5) Osduines Ogletree [b.Nov 1887]; (6) James E Ogletree [b.Oct 1896]; (7) Keattie Ogletree [female, b.Jun 1898]; (8) Walker Ogletree [b.Jun 1899]. Hattie does not appear (not yet born as of June 1900). This confirms Lewis Sr.'s parents and establishes siblings. Hattie Ogletree (b.~1900, Lewis Jr.'s 'Aunt' per WWII draft card) would be a younger sibling born after June 1900, consistent with this household's birth-order pattern. Extract to add family-of-origin context."

## Locality Guide: Spalding County, Georgia (1900–1930)

**Jurisdiction formed:** 20 December 1851 from Fayette, Henry, and Pike Counties. County seat: Griffin. No record loss from courthouse fires of 1874 or 1981 — all records survived.

**Neighboring counties:** Butts, Clayton, Coweta, Fayette, Henry, Lamar, Meriwether, Pike.

### Vital Records
*(Source: [Georgia Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Georgia_Vital_Records); [Spalding County, Georgia Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Spalding_County,_Georgia_Genealogy))*

| Type | Statewide Registration | General Compliance |
|------|----------------------|-------------------|
| Births | 1919 | 1928 |
| Deaths | 1919 | 1922 |
| Marriages | County-level from 1852; statewide 1952 | 1952 |

**Birth substitutes (pre-1919):** 1900, 1910, 1920 census; delayed birth affidavits (FS collection 3438747, indexed); church christening registers.

**Key birth/death collections on FamilySearch:**
- [Georgia, County Delayed Birth and Death Records, 1870–1960](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3438747) — index & images
- [Georgia, Deaths, 1914–1927](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1320969) — index & images
- [Georgia, Deaths, 1928–1943](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1385727) — index & images
- Georgia Archives Virtual Vault death certificates (1919–1930): https://vault.georgiaarchives.org/digital/collection/gadeaths/

### Marriage Records
**African American researchers:** Spalding County kept separate 'colored' marriage volumes:
- **Vol. F (1903–1910), colored** — imageGroup 007718973 — **100% indexed** ✅
- **Vol. I (1923–1933), colored** — imageGroup 007718976 — **100% indexed** ✅
- Vol. E (1898–1903): imageGroup 007718972 — **100% indexed** ✅
- Vol. G (1910–1917): imageGroup 007718974 — **100% indexed** ✅
- Vol. H (1917–1923): imageGroup 007718975 — **100% indexed** ✅

Statewide collections: [Georgia County Marriages 1785–1950](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1927197) (index & images); [Georgia Marriages 1808–1967](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1674807) (index only).

### Census Records
- **1900** (imageGroups 004120084_001, 004120083_004): **96–97% indexed** ✅
- **1910**: search via FS record search (national collection, well indexed) ✅
- **1920** (imageGroup 004300135): **0% indexed — browse-only** ❌
- **1930** (imageGroup 004532000): **0% indexed — browse-only** ❌

For 1920 and 1930, use Ancestry.com or MyHeritage where both years are indexed for Spalding County.

### Probate Records
- [Georgia, Probate Records, 1742–1990](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1999178) — index & images
- Spalding probate records (1892–1946): imageGroup 005782189 — **full-text searchable, not name-indexed**
- Will records (1929–1965): imageGroup 005782181 — **full-text searchable, not name-indexed**

### Newspapers / Obituaries
- *Griffin Daily News* and other local papers: [Digital Library of Georgia](https://gahistoricnewspapers.galileo.usg.edu/) — free access; [GenealogyBank](https://www.genealogybank.com/gbnk/newspapers/explore/USA/Georgia/) ($); Newspapers.com via Ancestry ($)
- Obituaries can name all surviving children — high priority for this question.

### Local Repositories
- **Georgia Archives**, 5800 Jonesboro Rd, Morrow, GA 30260 — statewide holdings
- **Griffin Spalding Historical Society**, 633 Meriwether St, Griffin, GA — local newspapers, family histories
- **Spalding County Courthouse**, 132 W. Solomon St., Griffin — court, land, and probate records from 1852
- Clerk Superior Court holds divorce and court records from 1852.

### African American Resources
See: [African American Resources for Georgia](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/African_American_Resources_for_Georgia). Key note: vital records and sometimes cemetery records for African Americans were kept in separate files with separate indexes — always search 'colored' or 'African American' sub-series specifically.
